task.name: The provider readiness check exercises a request shape no phase uses, so a model that fails every tool-bearing invocation is reported ready
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2377
---

**Depends on #2377.** That issue establishes which request shape serves a given capability for a given model and transport — the endpoint and effort setting under which a tool-bearing request is accepted. This issue's check has to exercise the shape a phase actually sends. Built before that contract exists, the check would probe the shape now known to be refused and would report failures for models that work correctly through the endpoint #2377 selects, replacing a false pass with a false fail.

## Observed

The provider readiness check reports a model healthy on the strength of a request shape the model is
never asked to serve in production.

The check issues a plain completion and reports a pass. Every phase that consumes a structured result
— plan review, code review, the escalation advisor — sends function tools instead. For one model
family the provider rejects tool-bearing requests outright while answering plain ones normally, so
the check returned a pass for two models that failed every tool-using phase they were routed to,
twenty-two times.

An operator enabling a model reads that pass as evidence the model works. It is evidence the model
answers, which is a different and much weaker claim. Nothing between the pass and the twenty-second
failure reported that the capability the model would actually be used for had never been exercised.

The same check also reports cost as unavailable for those models while reporting real figures for
others, so a second defect was visible in its output and likewise carried no consequence.

## Expected

A readiness check exercises the capabilities the checked thing will be asked to provide. Where a model
will be dispatched with tools, the check establishes that it accepts tools; where it will be asked for
a structured result, the check establishes that it can return one.

Where a capability cannot be exercised, the check reports that it was not exercised rather than
reporting a pass, so an operator can tell the difference between verified and untested.

A pass means the checked thing can do the jobs it is eligible for. Where a model is eligible for
phases with differing requirements, the result distinguishes which of those it can serve, so
eligibility can be narrowed to what was actually demonstrated rather than assumed from a single
minimal exchange.

## Diagnosis

**Observed symptom.** The readiness check passes a model that fails every tool-bearing invocation.

**Evidence.**

- The check reports a pass for two models of one family, with sub-5-second round trips.
- The same two models return 400 on every request carrying function tools, tracked separately as the
  transport-compatibility defect; run logs show 22 such rejections.
- Bisection confirms the boundary is tools specifically: plain and schema-constrained requests
  succeed against the same models, which is why a plain-completion probe cannot see it.
- The check's own output reports cost as unavailable for those models while showing figures for
  others, and that discrepancy is likewise carried without consequence.
- The models were enabled in project configuration on the strength of this pass, and the transport
  choice that caused the incompatibility was made in the same change.

**Ruled out.** Not a broken check: it performs the request it intends and reports the result truthfully.
Not provider flakiness, since the failure is deterministic by request shape. Not an authentication or
identifier error, both of which the check does detect.

**Confirmed cause.** The readiness probe exercises a single minimal request shape rather than the
capabilities a model is eligible to be dispatched with, so a model that answers but cannot serve any
tool-using phase is reported as ready.

**Affected code path.** The provider readiness check's probe construction and its pass criteria, and
the eligibility metadata a pass is taken to support.

**Fix-success criterion.** A model that cannot serve tool-bearing requests does not pass the readiness
check as ready for phases requiring tools, and any capability the check did not exercise is reported
as untested rather than folded into a pass.

handoff.summary: Implemented capability-level provider readiness probing so `forge check-providers` exercises the request shapes TheForge actually dispatches. The new helper derives probes from config roles, plan roles, the advisor shape, and adaptive agent-pool projections; preserves tool-bearing profiles instead of stripping tools; stamps plan and plan-review phases correctly; keeps role-distinct rows even for the same model/profile; and fail-closes unsupported OpenAI tool-bearing shapes via the #2377 request-shape contract. CLI tests and helper tests were updated accordingly, and a compatibility import was restored in `cli/providers.py` so the suite's autouse runner guard still patches the expected symbol.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5-cli] The change satisfies the provider-readiness acceptance criteria, and the authoritative gate for the reviewed HEAD passed. | [anthropic-opus-cli] Capability-level probing is correct and well tested, but the agent-dev probe now grants Write/Edit/Bash agent loops against the operator's project root, and the test-suite network guard no longer covers the real call site.

findings.description: Running the read-only diagnostic command check-providers now dispatches an agentic loop for every pooled model under the dev role, which resolves to the default dev tool surface including Write, Edit and Bash, and that loop executes against the directory containing forge.yaml, so a diagnostic invocation can create, modify or delete files and run shell commands in the operator's live project root.

The autouse test guard that blocks accidental real agent calls patches the symbol in the providers module, but the real call now happens through a separate binding in the readiness helper module, so a test that exercises check-providers without stubbing that helper reaches the network instead of failing loudly, while the retained unused re-export in providers makes the path look guarded.

The number of probes now scales with roles times pooled models — five probes per pooled agent plus the configured role probes — and every probe is given its own worker thread and runs a multi-turn tool loop rather than a single short completion, so a modest pool turns a previously cheap check into a large simultaneous burst of billed, long-running agent runs with no bound and no cost warning in the output.

Probes stamped with the dev and preflight phases are graded on returning a parseable object containing a verdict field, but those phases deliberately run without any forced-output or submit-tool contract in production, so a model that answers the probe in prose or in fenced JSON is reported as failed even though it serves those phases correctly.

findings.description: The capability narrowing that strips shell and write tools from a probe is applied only to the adaptive agent-pool dev role, so a dev profile declared directly in configuration under an API transport is still probed with its full declared surface including shell execution and file writing, while the pool-derived probe for the same conceptual role is restricted to reading.

The probe runner still accepts a working directory argument and the command still computes the project root and passes it in, but the value is never used because every probe now runs inside a freshly created temporary directory, so the signature advertises a control the caller does not actually have.

An untested status is declared and published in the exported status vocabulary, but no code path ever assigns it, so a consumer reading that vocabulary to enumerate possible outcomes is told about a state the check can never actually report.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 relies on iter_config_profiles for agent-pool coverage, but src/theforge/config/profiles.py calls agent.to_model_profile() with its default empty allowed_tools. Production adaptive routing instead uses assignment._agent_to_profile(), which supplies DEFAULT_DEV_PROFILE or DEFAULT_REVIEW_PROFILE tools and stamps the selected role. Consequently, an API model present through config.agents can still receive a plain readiness probe, pass, and later be routed into a tool-bearing dev, planner, plan-review, or code-review invocation—the exact false-pass condition this story must eliminate.
  Suggestion: Derive agent-pool probes for every production role/capability the agent can be assigned, using the same role projection contract as assignment._agent_to_profile, or mark those adaptive capabilities explicitly untested/non-ready. Add a test where a config.agents API model rejects tool-bearing requests and verify it cannot pass readiness merely because its iterator projection has an empty allowlist.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Stated risk 1 (no defined output vocabulary for untested vs unsupported) is only partially retired: the plan's mitigation fixes the CLI table shape but the plan names no single source for the label set, and Step 3/Step 4 assertions will each pick their own strings.
  Suggestion: Define the result states as an enum/constant tuple in src/theforge/cli/provider_readiness.py and have both providers.py rendering and the tests reference it, so the vocabulary cannot drift between helper and CLI.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4's unsupported-shape test cannot be written against real data as stated: _CHAT_COMPLETIONS_TOOL_UNSUPPORTED_MODELS (schema_utils.py:100) is deliberately empty, so no shipped model returns transport='unsupported'.
  Suggestion: Have the test monkeypatch the frozenset or the helper's shape lookup seam rather than naming a model string; do not add a real model to the fail-closed set just to make the test pass.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 adds 'unknown cost on a non-local endpoint' to the failure conditions, which changes the exit code for profiles that pass today (providers.py:126-131 currently prints '$?.???' with no consequence). This is what the spec asks for, but it will flip existing green runs to red.
  Suggestion: Ensure the cost-unavailable row is labelled distinctly from a capability failure in the table so an operator can tell the two apart at a glance, and mention the behaviour change in the commit body.

Probes stamped with the dev and preflight phases are graded on returning a parseable object containing a verdict field, but those phases deliberately run without any forced-output or submit-tool contract in production, so a model that answers the probe in prose or in fenced JSON is reported as failed even though it serves those phases correctly.

The probe runner still accepts a working directory argument and the command still computes the project root and passes it in, but the value is never used because every probe now runs inside a freshly created temporary directory, so the signature advertises a control the caller does not actually have.

An untested status is declared and published in the exported status vocabulary, but no code path ever assigns it, so a consumer reading that vocabulary to enumerate possible outcomes is told about a state the check can never actually report.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
